delivery_evidence_catalog.why_now: The survey note is the human-readable review anchor for the shipped starter packet and the remaining shared runtime-substrate blocker.
The module-slice note keeps the starter sample, loader scaffold, and bounded tests reviewable in one Phase 9 trace-events packet.
The dedicated survey gate fails closed when the manifest, note, loader scaffold, or trace-events build-step boundary drifts.
The focused `phase9-runtime-trace-events-tests` step inside the shared Phase 9 build bundle keeps the trace-events packet wired without claiming shared-loader ownership.

ownership_map.boundary: Records the shipped starter packet, points reviewers at the shared loader split, and keeps the remaining shared runtime-substrate blocker explicit.
Tracks the bounded starter sample, loader scaffold, and directly coupled tests without widening into shared runtime-loader ownership or runtime implementation.
Owns the in-memory trace-events starter and selftest hook without claiming live runtime-substrate parity.

Owns the sample-side loader-handoff scaffold, the prepared shared-request contract plus allocator-handoff and init-flow drift checks, the prepared shared selftest-hook drift checks before any local runtime handoff, the non-prepared shared-request rejection, the selftest-complete shared-request snapshot that stays pinned even after a later sample exit, and release-without-substrate behavior, while the shared runtime-loader lane owns the reusable facade, contract, and allocator replay surfaces it consumes.
Fail-closes when the trace-events manifest, survey note, loader scaffold, or focused Phase 9 trace-events build-step boundary drifts.

Owns only the `phase9-runtime-trace-events-tests` step in the shared Phase 9 replay bundle only while the shared loader lane keeps the facade, contract, allocator/init-flow replay, and `phase9-runtime-loader-shared-tests` step aligned.

gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step is the smallest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage from atomic64 and bitmap into the trace-events starter lane.
A trace-events survey gate keeps the Linux sample anchor, landed starter status, the bounded loader scaffold, and the remaining runtime-substrate blocker explicit while the pilot surface stays small.
A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing trace-events step that can model event emission and callback registration without pretending full macro or thread parity exists.
The Phase 9 roadmap explicitly calls for selftest hooks, and the bounded runtime_trace_events sample already keeps that requirement reviewable through descriptor metadata plus runSelftest().

A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, event emission counts, registration balance, and the new selftest rejection path when callback registration is already outstanding.
A narrow differential gate now captures a few foo_bar, template, and function-callback expectations from the Linux sample before any broader runtime substrate work.

A bounded sample-side loader scaffold now makes the existing requires_runtime_substrate contract reviewable through explicit tracepoint register and unregister APIs, prepared and initialized-stage handoff snapshots that stay stable even if later sample replay mutates local counters, a selftest-complete shared-request snapshot that stays pinned even if the sample exits before shared runtime handoff, prepared shared-request contract drift, allocator-handoff and init-flow drift checks, non-prepared shared-request rejection, and selftest-hook drift checks before any live handoff claim, shared release-failure guards that keep the local loader stage synchronized, and a no-substrate release path without pretending a real runtime loader already exists.

The roadmap's loadable runtime pilot module step still depends on a shared runtime substrate that can turn the bounded tracepoint_probe_register and tracepoint_probe_unregister handoff plan into a real loadable module path.
